#houseplants #pests

Fungus gnats, the sciarid sort, came in on a peace lily from the Co-op in September 2023 and by October were in every pot in the house, rising in a puff whenever I watered. The larvae live in the top few centimetres of wet compost and nibble fine roots. What worked, in order: let everything dry out properly between drinks (see [[Watering schedule]]); yellow sticky traps on sticks, a pack of 20 for £3.99, which caught 140 on the Monstera trap in a week; 1 cm of horticultural grit on top of each pot; and finally a pack of Steinernema feltiae nematodes (Nemasys, batch NF-2286, £12.99), watered in on 21 October 2023 at 14°C. Gone by mid November. They came back once in April 2025 after the repot in [[Monstera repotting]], so now any new compost goes in the freezer for 48 hours first.
